title: Number of Same-End Substrings
summary: Given a string s and a 2D array of queries, where each query specifies a substring of s from index l_i to r_i, return an array where each element represents the count of same-end substrings within the corresponding query's substring.
statement: Given a string s and a 2D array of queries, where each query specifies a substring of s from index l_i to r_i, return an array where each element represents the count of same-end substrings within the corresponding query's substring. A same-end substring has identical characters at both ends.
constraints: s has at least two lowercase letters and every query is an inclusive valid index pair.
A nonempty substring is same-end when its first and last characters match.
Return one count for each query range in the given order.
hints: For one character appearing c times in a range, choosing equal endpoints with repetition gives c(c+1)/2 substrings.
Build per-letter prefix counts, recover each query frequency vector, and sum the formula.
For every letter compute c=prefix[r+1]-prefix[l], then add c(c+1)/2.
Every same-end substring is uniquely identified by its endpoint character and ordered endpoint positions, including the same position twice.
editorial: Every same-end substring is uniquely identified by its endpoint character and ordered endpoint positions, including the same position twice.

tests.explanation: The four ranges contain respectively 1, 5, 5, and 10 same-end substrings.
All characters are distinct in either range, so only the four and two one-letter substrings qualify.
